messages.content: What wheather is now in Moscow, in celsius?

function.name: uber_eat_order
function.description: Place an order for food delivery on Uber Eats by specifying the restaurant and the items with their respective quantities. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

restaurant.description: The name of the restaurant from which to order food.

items.description: A list of food item names selected for the order.

quantities.description: A list of quantities for each food item, corresponding by index to the items array.

message.content: I’m sorry, but I don’t have access to live weather data. I can’t tell you the current temperature in Moscow right now. If you’d like, I can explain how to check it yourself using a weather website or app.

We don't have real-time data. We can approximate or say we can't fetch real-time data. But maybe we can use a weather API? There's no tool for that. We can respond that we cannot fetch real-time data. Or we can provide a placeholder. According to policy, we should not hallucinate. So we should say we don't have real-time data. Alternatively, we could ask for clarification. But likely we should respond that we cannot fetch real-time data.
